sample.name: California Theatre
facts: Opened in 1927 as a movie palace and closed in 1973.
Symphony San Jose moved into the restored theatre in 2004.
Home of Opera San José

sample.name: Guild
facts: The building opened in 1926 as the Menlo Theatre and was renamed the Guild in the late 1940s.
The Peninsula Arts Guild, led by Drew Dunlevie and backed by Pete Briger and Thomas Layton, drove the project.
Address: 949 El Camino Real, Menlo Park

sample.name: San Jose Improv Comedy Club
facts: The building opened in 1904 as the Jose Theater, the oldest theater in San Jose.
Construction began in 1903 under owner David Jacks, the Monterey landowner behind Monterey Jack cheese.
Address: 62 South 2nd Street, San Jose

sample.name: Montgomery Theater
facts: Built in 1936, the 500-seat theater is home to CMT San Jose.
Has a courtyard with a built-in fire pit that connects to the San Jose Civic courtyard.
Run by Team San Jose

sample.name: San Jose Stage Company
facts: Was the first group in San Jose to secure and manage its own theater facility.
Opened its 200-seat three-quarter thrust venue in 1990.
Address: 490 South 1st Street, San Jose

sample.name: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
facts: Opened in 1972 and designed by the Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation.
The theater has 2,608 seats, 1,852 orchestra and 756 balcony.
Designed by Taliesin Associated Architects

sample.name: San Jose Civic
facts: Opened in 1936, designed by Binder & Curtis in the Spanish California Mission style.
The Who launched their first headlining U.S. tour here in 1968.
Completed a renovation in 2012.
